'''Kyle Rittenhouse''' (born January 3, 2003) is an American figure who became widely known following his involvement in a high-profile shooting incident during the Kenosha unrest in August 2020. Rittenhouse was acquitted of all charges in November 2021, sparking significant media attention and public debate.

== Controversies ==
Rittenhouse has been a polarizing figure, often discussed in relation to gun rights and self-defense laws. His actions in Kenosha, where he fatally shot two individuals and injured another, sparked nationwide protests and discussions on racial justice, vigilantism, and the judicial system. Critics have accused Rittenhouse of acting recklessly, while supporters view him as a symbol of Second Amendment rights and self-defense.

== Conspiracies ==
Rittenhouse's trial and acquittal have been focal points for various conspiracy theories. Some of these theories incorrectly alleged that he was a member of extremist groups. Despite these claims, no credible evidence has substantiated such associations, and Rittenhouse has publicly denied any connections to such groups.

== Connection to Alex Jones ==
Following his trial, Rittenhouse appeared on ''The Alex Jones Show'' on September 18th, 2024. The appearance drew criticism from those wary of Jones' reputation and furthered discussions regarding Rittenhouse’s media engagements post-trial.
